$comment: The screen contract: which screens exist, what each one shows, and which operations in api.json it uses. web/src/router.tsx publishes the routes and every page is written against the row for it here.
$router_comment: Hash routing, so the server needs no history fallback and the app works inside the sandboxed preview frame.

screens.title: Your lists
screens.shows: Every list with how many of its tasks are still open, and a form that makes a new one.

screens.title: Tasks
screens.shows: The tasks in one list, a filter bar over status, search and tag, and a form that adds a task. The API does the filtering and the ordering.

screens.title: Overdue
screens.shows: Every open task across every list whose due date is strictly before today, most overdue first, with how many days late each one is.
screens.empty: Nothing is late. Every open task is due today or later.

TaskRow.shows: The title, the priority, the overdue badge when the task is late, the comment count when it has any, the due date and the tags.

OverdueBadge.shows: How many days late a task is. Renders nothing at all when the task is on time.

TaskFilters.shows: A status select, a search box and a tag box. Holds no state of its own.

NewTaskForm.shows: Title, priority, due date and tags, and whatever the API refused.

rules: The API filters and orders. Nothing in web/src filters an array that came back from the API, because the filter has to be right about the rows that were never downloaded.
The overdue rule lives in web/src/lib/overdue.ts and nowhere else. Every screen that needs it asks that function.
No cookies, no localStorage, no sessionStorage and no history.pushState. State is React state and the API, so the app works unchanged inside the preview's sandboxed frame.
